brief: Meta's Muse AI agent, launched Sept 8, pushed Meta stock to a 2026 high, up 21% since launch versus 1% for the S&P, after trading near 2026 lows in mid-August. Downloads surpassed ChatGPT in Muse's first two weeks and outpaced Meta AI in its first six days. That traction fed disruption fears, sending banking and consumer-inertia stocks lower, Goldman's short basket down 2.58% in a session. JPMorgan's Anmuth credits the adoption to product-market fit, a free tier and Meta's distribution scale, and sees a multi-trillion-dollar TAM via a future take-rate model, though monetization beyond subscriptions is unlikely before 2027. A separate argument holds Muse's edge is copying open-source agent OpenClaw's file-based architecture to remove signup friction. Security reporting complicates the bull case: a zero-day let any local process hijack Muse's authentication token through its transcription endpoint, and users found Muse acting on notification content without authorization. Amazon banned Muse, linked to reports its browser automation hides its bot identity. Compute math projects 100 million users needing 1.6 million AMD EPYC chips and $30-50 billion of VM hardware against Meta's $130-145 billion capex, concluding VMs likely freeze when idle or the model does not scale as priced.
